Q: Excel - paste special HTML option A:

This is maybe more code than you anticipated needing, but seems to function OK.

It uses Ron de Bruin's RangetoHTML function to create an HTML representation of the range to be copied, then adds a "wrapper" around that HTML before placing it on the clipboard. The "wrapper" around the HTML allows Excel to recognize that the clipboard has content in HTML format.

Background on the HTML "wrapper" at this link:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dataxchg/html-clipboard-format

See here for the RangetoHTML function:
https://jkp-ads.com/rdb/win/s1/outlook/bmail2.htm .

Sub TestCopyRangeAsHtml()
    
    Dim html As String, ws As Worksheet
    
    Set ws = ActiveSheet
    
    html = RangetoHTML(ws.Range("B2:E6")) 'See https://jkp-ads.com/rdb/win/s1/outlook/bmail2.htm
    set_clipboard_text wrapHTML(html)     'put wrapped HTML in the clipboard
    
    ws.Range("G2").Select    'must select before pasting
    ActiveSheet.PasteSpecial 'paste as HTML
End Sub

'See: https://stackoverflow.com/a/63735992/478884
'The "wrapper" lets Excel know the clipboard format is HTML
Private Function wrapHTML(ByVal html As String) As String
    Dim sData As String
    Const sContextStart = "<HTML><BODY><!--StartFragment -->"
    Const sContextEnd = "<!--EndFragment --></BODY></HTML>"
    Const sHtmlHeader = _
            "Version:1.0" & vbCrLf & _
            "StartHTML:<{]aaaaaaa" & vbCrLf & _
            "EndHTML:<{]bbbbbbb" & vbCrLf & _
            "StartFragment:<{]ccccccc" & vbCrLf & _
            "EndFragment:<{]dddddddd" + vbCrLf
    sData = sHtmlHeader & sContextStart & html & sContextEnd
    sData = Replace(sData, "<{]aaaaaaa", Format(Len(sHtmlHeader), "0000000000"))
    sData = Replace(sData, "<{]bbbbbbb", Format(Len(sData), "0000000000"))
    sData = Replace(sData, "<{]ccccccc", Format(Len(sHtmlHeader & sContextStart), "0000000000"))
    sData = Replace(sData, "<{]ddddddd", Format(Len(sHtmlHeader & sContextStart & html), "0000000000"))
    wrapHTML = sData
End Function

'https://stackoverflow.com/a/78329329/478884
Function set_clipboard_text(str_text)
    On Error GoTo err_handler
    Dim MSForms_DataObject As Object
    Set MSForms_DataObject = CreateObject("new:{1C3B4210-F441-11CE-B9EA-00AA006B1A69}")
    MSForms_DataObject.SetText str_text
    MSForms_DataObject.PutInClipboard
    Set MSForms_DataObject = Nothing
    set_clipboard_text = True
    Exit Function
err_handler:
    Debug.Print "error in set_clipboard_text function. Err: " & _
    Err.description
set_clipboard_text = False
End Function

Q: Unity NGO NetworkList of struct that contains an array of struct A:

See Arrays and native containers

You can basically go similar to the Job System and make use of Unity's struct based NativeArray for this.

Alternatively as mentioned on the page above you can also simply implement your own array like struct that implements INetworkSerializable which for your array would basically be something like

  • serialize length
  • then serialize flat out all elements

and for receiving wise versa

  • deserialize length
  • create empty array with according length
  • loop and deserialize the items

Q: Moshi 1.9.x Cannot serialize Kotlin type A:

https://www.baeldung.com/kotlin/sealed-class-serialization

Full example reproduced, below.

import com.squareup.moshi.Moshi
import com.squareup.moshi.adapters.PolymorphicJsonAdapterFactory
import com.squareup.moshi.kotlin.reflect.KotlinJsonAdapterFactory
import io.kotest.matchers.equals.shouldBeEqual
import kotlin.test.Test

sealed class Animal {
    abstract val name: String
    data class Dog(override val name: String, val breed: String) : Animal()
    data class Cat(override val name: String, val lives: Int) : Animal()
}

val moshi: Moshi = Moshi.Builder()
    .add(
        PolymorphicJsonAdapterFactory.of(Animal::class.java, "type")
            .withSubtype(Animal.Dog::class.java, "dog")
            .withSubtype(Animal.Cat::class.java, "cat")
    )
    .add(KotlinJsonAdapterFactory())
    .build()

class AdapterTest {
    @Test
    fun `serialize sealed class using moshi library`() {

        val dog = Animal.Dog("Buddy", "Labrador")
        val cat = Animal.Cat("Mike", 3)

        val jsonAdapter = moshi.adapter(Animal::class.java)

        dog shouldBeEqual jsonAdapter.fromJson(jsonAdapter.toJson(dog))!!
        cat shouldBeEqual jsonAdapter.fromJson(jsonAdapter.toJson(cat))!!
    }
}

Q: Can't figure out the real way to learn the C++ language? A:

Why don't you know where to start? It sounds like you had a specific experience with looking up information about span and saw something you didn't understand. What did you see? What terrified you about it? The example tries to implement 4 algorithms: slide, starts_with, ends_with, and contains by exercising span in a few different ways. Did you understand anything about the example? Find the first thing you don't understand and ask about that.

It sounds like you had an emotional response to it. That's valid. But you're moving the goalpost on your objective. Is the objective to "get up to speed"? Or is it to "learn about span"? Because the latter is totally doable, but "get up to speed" is possibly an unachievable objective. At best, it's under-defined. And that's likely like why you're feeling overwhelmed.

When it comes to learning, the objective shouldn't be to learn everything, it should just be to learn the next thing.

You already did the right thing to get started, which was to pick your next incremental step in your learning journey: span. That's great! But now go back and try again and get rid of the idea of "getting up to speed". That's what disrupted your learning. Ask specific targeted questions about specific things you don't understand. Don't be embarrassed about asking about things you don't understand even if it feels like the whole world gets it but you don't. If you're honest about what parts you do understand and what parts you don't understand then people can help you along in a way that feels like an achievable incremental step for you.

e.g.: (I don't know what the first thing you saw that left you stumped was, but maybe it's something like this:)

        if (auto s = slide(std::span{a}, offset, width); !s.empty())

Maybe you don't know what auto means? Maybe the {a} that follows std::span is a mystery. Or maybe you just got turned off by all the template code before we got to the meat of the example. I can only guess. But you should ask a specific question on stack overflow about it. For example say "I've seen auto s = foo() but never inside an if expression. What does that mean?" Or whatever it is that you saw that baffled you.
